reader.requirement: At --std 85 FACTORIAL's argument must be an integer argument (§1989:A.2.2 AR4: an arithmetic expression that always results in an integer value, so no scaled item, non-integral literal, numeric function, non-numeric operand or quotient not provably integral) and is refused otherwise; its >= 0 half is a value constraint whose violation makes the result undefined, and for 0 and positive values the factorial is returned.

reader.notes: The integer screen (IntegerViolation, fail-closed NotAlwaysIntegral) refuses every non-integer argument form at --std 85 exactly as at 2023, and admits integer items, literals, integer functions and provably integral expressions with correct values. The >= 0 half is not screened at compile time even for a literal -1; at 1985 it is a value constraint whose violation is undefined (§1989:A.2.2 AR4), so no refusal is required. Diagnostics at --std 85 cite §2023 clauses (15.36.3 r1).

refuter.evidence: fn_edge.cob at --std 85: COMPUTE R = FUNCTION FACTORIAL(N * (N + 1) / 2) with N PIC 99 is refused, EXIT 65, 'error COBOL1627: FUNCTION FACTORIAL argument-1 is an arithmetic expression whose term (N * (N + 1)) is an integer under the net factor 0.5, which is not a whole number, so the sum does not always result in an integer value'. N * (N + 1) is the product of two consecutive integers, always even, so the expression always results in an integer value for every valuation of N, exact under any intermediate precision; §1989:A.2.2 AR4 asks only that the expression 'will always result in an integer value' and sets no proof method, so this is legal source the compiler rejects. Same refusal at --std 2023 (fn_edge-002). The project records this class as debt itself: kb/Work PB5889 (decision, status open, rejects_legal_source: true) refuses integer arguments that are integers only by identity; this form is a sibling not listed there (integer terms under a non-whole net factor, not cancellation of non-integer terms). The rest of the reader's claim holds: fn_legal2.cob admits MAX(3 4), SUM(1 2), RANGE(1 5) (integer by argument types), a P-scaled PIC 9P item (10! = 3628800), 2 ** N, with correct values; fn_refuse2.cob refuses MAX(3 4.5), SUM(1 0.5), PIC P9, N ** -1; fn_float.cob refuses the 2002 floating literal 1.0E1 at 85 (COBOL0900). cite.py: OK §1989:A.2.2 AR4 'An arithmetic expression which will always result in an integer value must be specified'; OK §1989:A.2.14.3 AR1 'Argument-1 must be an integer greater than or equal to zero'.
